AdVenture Capitalist is an idle progress game by Hyper Hippo Games. While it exists in many formats including Android, PC through Steam, and even a web app on Kongregate, I am specifically reviewing it for iOS using an iPad Air 2.

AdVenture Capitalist is a fairly standard idle game- several different progress bars (companies) develop at different speeds, and complete to give you money. You use the money to buy more of a company or to buy upgrades for the group, naturally makes you more money to continue along. You can also buy managers that give special improvements to a business, such as automatically starting the progress bar, drastically lowering the price, or showing income in seconds instead of pulses. There is also a restart mechanic called Angel Investors, that you build up as you make more money. They offer a base increase in money per pulse, and can also be spent for upgrades and managers. Anyone who has played Idle Oil Tycoon will notice the game is practically a reskin, and this bugged me at first.

However, AC has brought a number of improvements to the table over IOT. AC has a much prettier interface, and the overall experience is more smooth and interesting for the player. In AC, you can also earn your way to operating a second, more difficult set of businesses on the moon. They are completely separated from the other set of businesses in that they use their own currency and can be reset independently. Otherwise, they operate on all the same principles as the core game.

Another major difference between AC and IOT is in monetization. IOT used splash ads each time you opened the game, with an option to buy a permanent manager to stop the ads. AC gives you the option to watch a video, at the end of which you gain double your income for 4 hours, up to five times a day. The moon expansion has a separate video option as well, which I personally think is a bit crappy. It's better than inline ads or splash ads though, so I won't complain too loudly. What really bothers me is the gold. You can buy in game currency to get special upgrades and bonuses. I haven't tested this myself, but it appears that these upgrades do not live past a reset. To me, this comes off as being really scummy. It doesn't make the game unplayable to ignore it though, and up until writing this review, I had actually forgotten the option was there.

AC is still very much a game in development. There are several features that are clearly just there for future development, and I do still run into the occasional bug. The worst one I've seen is after playing the ads, if my screen is horizontal the entire interface tries to refit as if it were vertical, and makes the game unplayable until I reset.

Overall, the game is fine. Being an idle game I can't call it fun, but it does the job it intends to do quite satisfactorily. While it has problems, it delivers on the promise of a game of basic strategic upgrading with a monetization platform that doesn't saturate the gameplay. You could do much worse than AdVenture Capitalist to fill your idle needs.
